summary: Flathead National Forest pole lookout built in 1937 and abandoned in 1949; listed as gone, and no source describes the site today.

facts.status_note: Abandoned in 1949 and listed as gone. No source we read describes the site today.

evidence.supports: location: about 24 miles east-northeast of Spotted Bear Ranger Station
evidence.quote: 24 miles ENE of Spotted Bear R.S.

evidence.supports: fire-detection points on high peaks after the 1910 fire season
evidence.quote: After the 1910 fire season, the Forest Service went on the offensive, setting up fire detection points on high peaks

evidence.supports: lookouts added especially in the 1930s; 147 lookouts and towers by 1939
evidence.quote: The Forest built more and more lookouts, especially during the 1930s, until in 1939 there were 147 lookouts and towers on the Flathead National Forest

evidence.supports: list marks the site as a gone tower

sources.title: Trails of the Past: Historical Overview of the Flathead National Forest, Montana, 1800-1960, Chapter 9

notes_for_editor: The build year (1937), the 20-foot pole L-4 tower, the 1949 abandonment and the elevation rest on one short firelookout.com page; the Forest Association list row confirms only the Flathead County location and gone status. Two web searches found no staffing, fire or present-day site records. The 1939 lookout count and the detection-point context come from the Flathead National Forest history chapter and are background, not facts about this site. Record coordinates match the list row.
